name: uscope
description: Debug native Linux programs written in C, C++, Rust, Go, and Zig with uscope

uscope.path.markdownDescription: The `uscope` executable: a name searched for on `PATH`, or a path, which may start with `${workspaceFolder}` or `${userHome}`. Relative paths start at the workspace folder.

uscope.hexadecimal.markdownDescription: Show integers in hexadecimal in the Variables and Watch views, hovers, and the results of expressions in the debug console; commands such as `print/x` choose their own. *Toggle Hexadecimal Display* in the Variables and Watch views' context menus flips it.

uscope.logFile.markdownDescription: A file the adapter appends every protocol message to, for reporting problems: `uscope dap --log`. It may start with `${workspaceFolder}` or `${userHome}`. Empty logs nothing.

cwd.description: The program's working directory. Defaults to the adapter's.

env.description: Environment variables set over the adapter's environment; null removes one.

stopOnEntry.description: Stop at the program's first instruction, in the dynamic loader.

followForks.description: Debug each process the program forks in a session of its own, which stops at its breakpoints. Otherwise children run on their own.

enumDescriptions: The program's output appears in the debug console, and its input is empty.
The program runs in the integrated terminal, which owns its input and output.
The program runs in an external terminal, which owns its input and output.
console.description: Where the program's standard streams go.

sourceMap.description: Rules that read source files recorded under one path from another: [["/build/src", "${workspaceFolder}/src"]]. Earlier rules are tried first.

viewFiles.description: View files that present values, ahead of the project's .uscope/views, the user's, the program's own, and the built-in views. Later files come first.

debugDirectories.description: Directories searched for the separate debug files of stripped modules, by build-id under .build-id and by .gnu_debuglink, before NIX_DEBUG_INFO_DIRS and /usr/lib/debug.

debuginfod.description: Download debug files no directory holds from the debuginfod servers DEBUGINFOD_URLS lists, keeping them in debuginfod's cache.

disassemblySyntax.description: The assembly syntax of the disassembly view.

threads.description: Show a runtime's tasks, such as Go's goroutines, as threads, or the system threads.

runtimeTasks.description: List the tasks a runtime runs for its own work, such as Go's garbage collector workers.

maxTasks.description: The most tasks listed as threads; a last entry says how many more there are.

stepIntoRuntime.description: Let steps stop in a language runtime's own code, such as Go's or tokio's, rather than pass over it.

signals.description: How each signal is handled, over the exception filters: stop, nostop, print, noprint, pass, or nopass, such as {"SIGUSR1": "nostop"}.

pid.description: The process to attach to. ${command:pickProcess} picks one when the session starts.

coreFile.description: A core dump to open instead of a process.

program.description: The process's or core dump's executable, when it cannot be found automatically. With ${command:pickProcess}, the picker lists only processes running it.

stopOnEntry.description: Stay stopped after attaching instead of continuing the process.

followForks.description: Debug each process the program forks in a session of its own, which stops at its breakpoints. Otherwise children run on their own.

sysroot.description: A copy of the files of the machine that wrote the core dump, in which its module paths are looked up.

modulePaths.description: Directories searched for core dump modules missing from their recorded paths.

allowModuleMismatch.description: Use module files that cannot be proven to match the core dump.
